messages:
alex_m: Quick sync — follow-up to the continuous-batcher RFC. I want to capture tradeoffs between a prefetch / windowed admission approach vs strict token-affinity lanes. Throwing up some notes and questions.

jing: SGTM. can you list the primary failure/misbehavior modes we care about?

alex_m: sure — off the top of my head: long-tail latency spikes when a big request blocks a batch, increased memory/KV pressure from aggressive prefetch, tenant unfairness (large vs small requests), and complexity of eviction logic when we prefetch partial KV.

sukh: also operational surface: observability for prefetch hits/misses, telemetry for affinity collisions, and toggles for per-tenant priorities.

maria: i'd add: degradation modes when quantized kernels change throughput characteristics mid-batch (we saw this with v2 quant tests). Prefetch can make this worse because you commit GPU memory earlier. :grimacing:

alex_m: right. thinking about two concrete designs: A) Prefetch-window: accept requests into a short window (eg 5–20ms) and prefetch keys for early arrivals; batches formed from window. B) Affinity-lanes: classify by token-affinity (prefix similarity, KV overlap) and schedule into small lanes pinned to worker islands to avoid KV churn.

jing: quick tradeoffs I see: Prefetch-window is simpler and maximizes throughput with continuous batching, but increases wasted prefetch work. Affinity lanes reduce KV swapping but can underutilize GPU if lanes go idle.

ops_lead: from SLO POV, prefetch-window increases p50 and p95 predictability but might push p99 if prefetch evictions happen. lanes give tighter p99 for similar requests but harder tail isolation across tenants.

sukh: experiment idea: run both under synthetic mix (50% short, 20% long, 30% medium) and track: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, KV cache hit rate, GPU mem delta, and fairness (service rate per-tenant).

maria: + add a synthetic stress with quantized model step-change to validate eviction resilience. Also measure CPU overhead for scheduling decisions.

alex_m: implementation notes: Prefetch-window needs: prefetch_window_ms config, a timer wheel per-queue, prefetch worker that materializes KV into a shareable region, and an eviction policy tuned for async prefetch. Affinity-lanes needs: fast affinity hashing (e.g., bloom of prefix tokens), mapping function -> lane, and lane-local KV that is sticky.

jing: small concern: lane stickiness can create hot lanes. we need a migration policy to rebalance without causing cache storms. maybe allow lane-splitting when backlog > X.

sukh: agree. propose heuristics: split if queue_length > split_threshold AND avg_batch_util < util_threshold. merge if idle for T_merge. Keep it simple to start.

alex_m: psuedocode for admission (prefetch-window):

```
on_request(req):
  queue.append(req)
  if window_timer not set:
    set_timer(prefetch_window_ms)

on_timer():
  batch = queue.drain(max_batch_size)
  prefetch(batch.keys)
  dispatch(batch)
```

maria: looks fine. we should also record per-batch prefetch_bytes and prefetch_latency metrics so optimize prefetch_window_ms automatically later.

ops_lead: who owns the experiment? i can pair infra with runtime to run in staging and gate by tenant-sim harness.

alex_m: ops_lead + s ukh to run initial runs next week. Jing/maria to define telemetry dashboards and experiment queries (p50/p95/p99, kv_hit, prefetch_wasted_bytes).

sukh: one more: safety fallback — if prefetch_eviction_rate > X% or gpu_mem_pressure spikes, immediately switch to conservative mode: prefetch_window_ms=0 (disable) and enable greedy lane-merging. Add a circuit-breaker metric.

jing: love that. also add an annotation in traces when mode switches so we can correlate client errors.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline: staging/continuous-batcher-experiments -> rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% gated on p99 < baseline * 1.2 and kv_hit >= baseline - 0.1.

maria: small ask: add a per-tenant override so enterprise customers can opt-out of prefetch to preserve determinism.

alex_m: agreed. i'll draft the RFC follow-up with experiment plan, config knobs (prefetch_window_ms, split_threshold, merge_idle_ms, affinity_hash_bits, per_tenant_optout) and expected telemetry. Posting first sketch in #eng-runtime-docs by EOD.

ops_lead: ack. ping here when it's up and we'll schedule the runs. :thumbsup:

alex_m: thanks all. closing notes: focus on measurable hypotheses, start with prefetch-window as low-risk default, and iterate affinity lanes if we see cache churn that prefetch can't handle.

jing: SGTM.
